verdict.rationale: The evidence shows Khoj can be self-hosted and keep data and embeddings on the user's machine. Nothing documents a memory store of what the assistant has remembered, nor any way to inspect, edit, or delete those memories, nor an open storage format. Self-hosting and local embeddings are adjacent privacy features, not the memory-management capability this story asks for.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, I can inspect, edit, and delete what the assistant has remembered — the memory store lives on my machine in an open format
